messages.subject: Packages/libraries for audio identification/segmentation
parts:
Hi everyone,

I'm working on a research project to be able to identify, label, and/or segment the individual notes in audio recordings of bird songs (the Cassin's Finch specifically). I have .wav files of each possible individual note that has been previously identified but have many recordings that need to still be labeled with their respective notes. Currently I've been trying to work with a Python package called pyAudioAnalysis that would theoretically allow me to feed in the .wav files of the individual notes to train the program to identify them in larger recordings of songs that have not yet had their notes labeled. However, this has been rife with issues and I was wondering if there was anything R-based that could perform a similar function of identifying, labeling, and/or segmenting these audio files. 

The ultimate goal is to have a large collection of each note from different individuals identified and separated. Because male Cassin's Finches display the unique behavior of utilizing pieces of other birds' songs in their own, presumably for the purpose of mating, the goal is to create audio files composed of these separated notes that will be played back to female Cassin's Finches to see how they respond to different compositions of notes.

Hopefully the question and purpose of the project make sense, but please feel free to ask if anything needs clarification. Thank you for your help!

All the best,

Parish Bracha

messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Packages/libraries for audio identification/segmentation
parts:
Hi Parish,
I don't have direct experience with audio signal processing, beyond reading a few journal articles, covering topics such as remote monitoring of tropical frog diversity, and shot-mapping in predictive policing.
I do, however, have experience processing hyperspectral remote sensing imagery, and there are some similarities in the preprocessing and classification procedures (light in spatial domain vs. sound in time domain)

A quick Google search turned up the following:

https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/soundgen/vignettes/acoustic_analysis.html 

 https://medium.com/@taposhdr/basics-of-audio-file-processing-in-r-81c31a387e8e

http://samcarcagno.altervista.org/blog/basic-sound-processing-r/?doing_wp_cron=1580186288.8119649887084960937500 

Best of luck in your project.

Zack Silber-Coats
